title: Sausage Egg Bake
subtitle: Morning feed after night shift
description: Morning feed after night shift. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.instruction: Cook sausage in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it into small crumbles, 8–10 minutes until fully browned. Drain well and let cool slightly.

steps.title: Layer the base
steps.instruction: Spread thawed hash browns across the bottom of two greased baking dishes. Scatter browned sausage and diced onion evenly over the top.

steps.title: Whisk and pour the custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs, milk, dry mustard, and salt until smooth. Pour evenly over the hash browns and sausage; sprinkle cheddar over the top.

steps.title: Rest before baking
steps.instruction: Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour, overnight works well, so the hash browns soften and the flavors settle.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Bake uncovered at 350°F for 45–55 minutes until the center is fully set with no jiggle and the top is golden. Internal temperature should read at least 160°F.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares — this keeps portions clean instead of falling apart on the spatula.

proTips: Firefighters eat heavy after rough nights — double the protein if the hall had a busy shift.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Sausage Egg Bake with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Serve family-style from two full-size trays — never let the line run dry on a busy night.
Put starch and protein on separate trays so vegetarians can load up on sides.
Line up Sausage Egg Bake on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Morning feed after night shift. A hall pick for big-appetite nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.

adaptable.label: Dairy-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use oat, almond, or soy milk (check tree-nut/soy status of the substitute). Use a dairy-free cheese shred/block alternative.

adaptable.label: Pork-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Swap in chicken or turkey sausage.
